application.name: IncomingOrderProcessor
application.description: A Windows Service that processes incoming orders from Microsoft Message Queuing (MSMQ)

legacyPatterns.description: Application is built as a Windows Service, which is not cloud-native
legacyPatterns.azureReplacement: Azure Container Apps, Azure Functions, or Azure Service Bus triggered applications

legacyPatterns.description: Uses MSMQ for message queuing, which is Windows-specific and not available in Azure
legacyPatterns.azureReplacement: Azure Service Bus, Azure Queue Storage, or Azure Event Hubs

legacyPatterns.description: Uses classic .NET Framework project format (non-SDK style)

legacyPatterns.azureReplacement: Configuration-driven Azure Service Bus queue/topic connection

blockers: Windows Service architecture not supported in Azure PaaS services
MSMQ dependency requires Windows Server (IaaS) or migration to Azure messaging services
.NET Framework 4.8.1 is Windows-only and not cross-platform
concerns: No health checks or monitoring endpoints
strengths: Simple, focused application with clear responsibility
Good error handling in message processing

targetServices.service: Azure Container Apps or Azure Functions
targetServices.purpose: Replace Windows Service with cloud-native compute
Store container images if using Container Apps

migrationSteps.name: Replace MSMQ with Azure Service Bus
migrationSteps.description: Refactor message queue integration to use Azure Service Bus SDK

migrationSteps.name: Convert Windows Service to cloud-native host
migrationSteps.description: Refactor from Windows Service to Worker Service or Azure Functions

migrationSteps.name: Add configuration management
migrationSteps.description: Implement Azure App Configuration or environment-based configuration

migrationSteps.name: Add telemetry and monitoring
migrationSteps.description: Integrate Application Insights for logging and monitoring

migrationSteps.name: Deploy to Azure
migrationSteps.description: Deploy to Azure Container Apps or Azure Functions

securityConsiderations.recommendation: Use environment variables or Azure App Configuration
Implement Azure Service Bus with managed identity

securityConsiderations.concern: Console logging may expose sensitive order data
securityConsiderations.recommendation: Implement structured logging with PII redaction

recommendations.recommendation: Upgrade to .NET 8 or .NET 9 for cross-platform support and long-term support
Migrate from MSMQ to Azure Service Bus for cloud-native messaging
Refactor from Windows Service to Azure Container Apps or Azure Functions
Implement configuration management using Azure App Configuration or environment variables
Add Application Insights for monitoring, logging, and telemetry
Use Azure Key Vault for secrets and Managed Identity for authentication
Add unit tests and integration tests
Containerize the application for deployment flexibility

summary.currentState: Legacy Windows Service using MSMQ on .NET Framework 4.8.1
summary.targetState: Cloud-native microservice on .NET 8/9 using Azure Service Bus, deployed to Azure Container Apps
summary.recommendedApproach: Modernize and migrate with architectural changes
